mainTopic: Identifying the סריס חמה and the אילונית, רבי אליעזר's seemingly conflicting rulings, and how late signs of maturity affect a person's status
overview: The amud opens by finishing the definition of a סריס חמה: a man who never had even one moment of being able to have children. אביי gives a sign we can see to identify him, and the גמרא explains that the defect starts in the womb. The גמרא asks whether he might have been healed for a while in between. It answers that a defect of the whole body, present at birth and still present now, is assumed to have lasted the whole time; only a blemish on one limb needs checking again and again. Next the גמרא points out that רבי אליעזר seems to contradict himself, comparing our משנה with a משנה in נדה about one who never matured. שמואל's answer, quoted by רמי בר דיקולי, is that רבי אליעזר changed his mind, and a ברייתא shows he kept his view that a סריס חמה does חליצה. רבי אלעזר answers differently: the משנה in נדה is only about punishments. This leads to an argument between רב and שמואל about a boy who matured late. אביי defends רב by explaining that an אילונית goes straight from minor to full adult, and a ברייתא backs him up. Finally, רבי אבהו says we do not act on these signs until age twenty. The גמרא then questions whether a baby born in the eighth month can even live, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Defining the man born infertile
steps.stepSummary: The definition of a סריס חמה ends here: he never had a single moment of being able to have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...who never saw a single hour in his fitness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a definition that began before this section. The person being described never had even one moment of being healthy and able to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the key test for a סריס חמה. It is not enough that he cannot have children now. He must have been this way from birth, without any healthy moment at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A man born unable to father children
Fitness; here, being able to have children

phrases.english: who never saw a single hour in his fitness.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before this section, which describes the סריס חמה, the man born infertile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the definition from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סריס חמה is someone who never had even one moment of being able to have children.

steps.title: How can we tell he was born this way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can know that a man was never able to have children, even for a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: how do we recognize such a person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition depends on his whole life since birth, and we cannot see that directly. So we need some sign we can see now that tells us he was born this way.

phrases.english: How do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to identify the person defined in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A sign that shows a man was infertile from birth.

steps.title: אביי's sign: no arch when urinating
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the sign is a man whose urine does not form an arch.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Anyone who passes water and does not make an arch.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with a physical sign. If a man's urine dribbles down instead of shooting out in an arch, he was never able to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign is something we can see now, and it tells us about his condition from birth. This makes the definition from step 1 usable in practice.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Anyone who passes water
and does not make an arch.
phrases.notes: He means the urine dribbles straight down instead of curving outward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A man whose urine does not form an arch was infertile from birth.

steps.title: What causes this condition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks, as a side question, what causes this defect.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what does it come about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside for a moment and asks what causes a baby to be born this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question does not change the הלכה. It adds background about where the condition comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From what does it come about?

phrases.english: From what does it come about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about the cause of the condition described in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The cause of being born infertile.

steps.title: The mother baking at noon and drinking strong beer
steps.stepSummary: The cause is the mother baking at midday and drinking strong beer while she was pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: That his mother baked at noon and drank strong beer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the condition comes from what the mother did while pregnant: she baked in the heat of midday and drank strong beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer places the cause before birth, while he was still inside his mother. This fits the idea that the defect was there from the very start of his life.

phrases.english: That his mother baked at noon
and drank strong beer.
phrases.notes: This happened while she was pregnant with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mother baked at noon and drank strong beer during the pregnancy.

steps.title: רב יוסף finally understands רבי אמי's words
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says this explains a phrase he heard from רבי אמי, 'anyone impaired from his mother's womb,' which he had not understood before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is what I heard from רבי אמי, who said 'anyone who is impaired from his mother's womb,' and I did not know what it was.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף connects this teaching to something he once heard from רבי אמי. Now he understands it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי spoke of someone 'impaired from his mother's womb.' רב יוסף now sees that this means the man born infertile, whose defect began during the pregnancy. This gives the idea backing from an earlier teacher.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
This is what I heard from Ami, who said:
"Anyone who is impaired from his mother's womb,"
and I did not know what it was.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הַיְינוּ דְּשָׁמַעְנָא לְאִמִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports steps 3 and 5 by linking them to רבי אמי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That the man born infertile is impaired from the womb.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אמי's phrase 'anyone who is impaired from his mother's womb.'

steps.title: Maybe he was healed for a while in between
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we should worry that he was healed at some point between birth and now.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that perhaps he became healthy in between!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the sign. The man may have had a healthy period in the middle that we never knew about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition requires that he never had even one healthy moment. If he was healed for a while, he would not count as a סריס חמה, even though he is impaired now.

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he became healthy in between!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main line, the sign from step 3, and questions whether it proves the definition in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the present sign to decide that he was never healthy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being impaired now and at birth does not rule out a healthy period in the middle, and that period would disqualify him from the definition.

steps.title: Impaired at the start and the end, so no worry
steps.stepSummary: Since he was impaired at birth and is still impaired now, we do not worry about a healthy period in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since his beginning and his end are impaired, we do not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that if the defect was there at the beginning and is still there now, we assume it lasted the whole time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the start, because the cause happened in the womb. We also know the end, because we can see the sign now. With both ends the same, we do not invent a hidden healthy period in the middle.
steps.whatToRemember: If this kind of defect is there at birth and is still there now, we assume it lasted the whole time in between. Step 10 explains that this applies to a defect of the whole body, not to a blemish on one limb.

phrases.english: Since his beginning and his end are impaired —
we are not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Presumption: the same state at both ends means the same state throughout.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might worry about a hidden healthy period in the middle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being impaired at the beginning and at the end removes that worry.

steps.title: רב מרי challenges from checking a blemish three times
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי challenges from the view of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס that a blemish must be checked three times within eighty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי raised an objection: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: We examine it three times within eighty days!
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי brings a source that seems to disagree with the answer in step 8. There, a defect is checked several times during the period, not only at the beginning and the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being impaired at the start and the end were enough, there would be no reason to check three times. Requiring several checks suggests we do worry that the defect healed in the middle.

phrases.english: Rav Mari raised an objection:
Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:
We examine it three times
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בכורות about a firstborn animal with a blemish in its eye. "It" means that animal.

phrases.english: within eighty days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that being impaired at the beginning and at the end means we do not worry.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Checking three times during the period shows that we do worry about healing in the middle, even when the defect is there at the beginning and at the end.

steps.title: One limb versus the whole body
steps.stepSummary: We worry that a blemish came and went only when it affects a single limb. We do not worry about this when the defect affects the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a single limb we are concerned; for the whole body we are not concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב מרי's challenge from רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. That rule about checking a blemish over time applies only to a blemish on one limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish on one limb, like an eye, can heal and come back, so it needs to be checked over time. A סריס is not impaired in just one limb; his whole body is affected. So if he was impaired at birth and is impaired now, we do not worry that he was healthy for a while in between.

keyTerms.meaning: we are concerned / we take into account

steps.whatToRemember: A defect that affects the whole body is treated as lasting. Only a single-limb blemish raises the worry that it healed and came back.

phrases.english: With a single limb, we are concerned,
phrases.notes: He means we worry that this kind of blemish went away and came back, so it needs checking.

phrases.english: with the whole body, we are not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְחַד אֵבֶר חָיְישִׁינַן, לְכוּלֵּיהּ גּוּפָא לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מרי's challenge in Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (single limb versus whole body)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every blemish needs repeated checking because it might have healed in between, as רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says.
steps.terutzMaskana: Repeated checking applies only to a single-limb blemish. A whole-body defect like סריס is not suspected of healing in between.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר and bringing a contradicting משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view in our משנה and sets up a contradiction from a משנה in נדה about a man or woman who never showed signs of maturity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: No, etc. They raised a contradiction: A twenty-year-old man who did not grow two hairs: they must bring proof that he is twenty, and he is the סריס, so he does not do חליצה or יבום. A twenty-year-old woman who did not grow two hairs: they must bring proof that she is twenty, and she is the איילונית, so she does not do חליצה or יבום. These are the words of בית הלל. בית שמאי say: for both, the age is eighteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new section of our משנה, רבי אליעזר's view, and starts quoting a משנה that seems to contradict him. This step sets up the contradiction; the key line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי אליעזר holds that a סריס חמה, a man impaired from birth, does do חליצה. The משנה in נדה teaches that a man who never matured by twenty is a סריס and does not do חליצה or יבום. בית הלל and בית שמאי argue only about the age, twenty or eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: two hairs, the sign of physical maturity
a man without the ability to have children
a woman who never matured and cannot have children

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר לֹא כִּי וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: No, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, where רבי אליעזר says a סריס חמה does do חליצה.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
A twenty-year-old man
who has not grown two hairs
they must bring proof that he is twenty,
and then he is the סריס,
he does not do חליצה and does not do יבום.

phrases.aramaic: בַּת עֶשְׂרִים וְלֹא הֵבִיאָה שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת
phrases.english: A twenty-year-old woman who has not grown two hairs
they must bring proof that she is twenty,
and then she is the איילונית,
she does not do חליצה and does not do יבום,
these are the words of בית הלל.
And בית שמאי say:
For both this one and that one, the age is eighteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section of the משנה (רבי אליעזר's view) and starts a contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling in our משנה that a סריס חמה does חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in נדה treats a man who never matured as a סריס who does not do חליצה; the next step shows that רבי אליעזר agrees with this.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's view in the contradicting משנה
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה in נדה, רבי אליעזר takes part in the argument about age and accepts that one who never matured does not do חליצה. This clashes with his view in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: For a male, follow בית הלל, and for a female, follow בית שמאי, because a woman matures faster than a man!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the contradiction. רבי אליעזר himself argues only about the age, so he agrees that a natural סריס does not do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר only splits the age question: twenty for a man, eighteen for a woman, because women mature sooner. He does not disagree with the basic rule that a natural סריס does not do חליצה. In our משנה, though, he says a סריס חמה does do חליצה, so his two statements seem to contradict each other.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not mention חליצה in this line. The contradiction comes from the fact that he joins the argument about age and does not object to the ruling that a natural סריס does not do חליצה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The male is according to the words of בית הלל,
phrases.notes: For a man, the age is twenty.

phrases.english: and the female is according to the words of בית שמאי,
phrases.notes: For a woman, the age is eighteen.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה מְמַהֶרֶת לָבֹא לִפְנֵי הָאִישׁ!
phrases.english: because a woman matures faster than a man!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הַזָּכָר כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction set up in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling in our משנה that a סריס חמה does חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In נדה, רבי אליעזר argues only about the age and accepts that a natural סריס does not do חליצה. In our משנה he says a סריס חמה does do חליצה, so his two statements conflict.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר took back one of his statements
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר דיקולי, quoting שמואל, resolves the contradiction: רבי אליעזר changed his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר דיקולי said in the name of שמואל: רבי אליעזר retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רבי אליעזר did once hold both views, but he later took one of them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of finding a difference between the two cases, this answer says the two statements come from different times. One of them is no longer רבי אליעזר's final view. This answer does not say which one, which leads to the next question.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר דִּיקּוּלֵי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rami bar Dikulei said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Eliezer retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Steps 11-12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the two statements come from different times
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר holds two conflicting views at the same time.
steps.terutzMaskana: He took one of them back, so only one is his final view.

steps.title: Which statement did he take back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of רבי אליעזר's two statements he took back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: From which did he retract?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: did רבי אליעזר take back his view in our משנה or his view in the משנה in נדה? The next step will try to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said that רבי אליעזר changed his mind but not which view he dropped. If he took back our משנה, then a סריס חמה does not do חליצה even according to him. If he took back the משנה in נדה, his view in our משנה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked before them
from which statement did he retract?

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
From which one did he retract?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about the answer in Step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר took back his ruling in our משנה or his position in the משנה in נדה

steps.title: A ברייתא shows he kept his view on the סריס חמה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי אליעזר saying a סריס חמה does חליצה, with a reason: people like him are cured in Alexandria. So he kept this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: A סריס חמה does חליצה, and his brothers do חליצה with his wife, because people of this type are healed in Alexandria of Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. It shows that רבי אליעזר stood by his view in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats רבי אליעזר's view that a סריס חמה does חליצה and gives a reason: his condition can be cured, as is done in Alexandria. Since he holds this view with a stated reason, he probably did not take it back. That means he took back what he said in the משנה in נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: a סריס from birth, by natural causes

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, רבי אליעזר's final view is that a סריס חמה does חליצה, because his condition can be cured. The statement he took back is the one in the משנה in נדה.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A סריס חמה does חליצה,
and they do חליצה with his wife,
phrases.notes: If he dies childless, his brothers do חליצה with his widow.

phrases.english: because people of their type are healed
in Alexandria of Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 14 using a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר kept his view that a סריס חמה does חליצה, so the statement he took back is the one in the משנה in נדה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason given, that the condition can be cured, explains why רבי אליעזר treats a סריס חמה as able to do חליצה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: He Never Changed His Mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר gives a different answer: רבי אליעזר never took back either view, because the משנה in נדה is only about punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: In fact, he never changed his mind. And when we learned that משנה, it was about punishments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the contradiction from Step 12. רבי אלעזר says there is no contradiction at all, so רבי אליעזר never needed to change his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר דיקולי said רבי אליעזר took back one of his rulings. רבי אלעזר says both rulings stand, because they deal with different topics. The age rules in the משנה in נדה only decide when such a person can be punished for sins, not whether he does חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth (here it means 'really, after all')
He did not take back his words
Punishments: the age when a person becomes liable for his sins

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אלעזר, who is speaking here, with רבי אליעזר, whose view is being discussed. The names look almost the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Actually, he did not take back his view.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אליעזר, whose two statements seemed to clash.

phrases.english: And when we learned that משנה,
phrases.notes: "That" is the משנה in נדה about one who never showed signs of maturity.

phrases.english: it was about punishments.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם לָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction that רמי בר דיקולי answered by saying רבי אליעזר changed his mind.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the topics: the two rulings deal with different areas of law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the age rules in the משנה in נדה apply to חליצה too, so they clash with our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The age rules in נדה are only about when one can be punished, so both of רבי אליעזר's views stand.

steps.title: רב and שמואל Argue About Late Signs of Maturity
steps.stepSummary: A boy sinned between ages 12 and 18, showed signs of a סריס, and later grew two hairs. רב says he is a סריס from the start; שמואל says he was a minor when he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: If someone ate חלב between age twelve and a day and age eighteen, and signs of a סריס appeared in him, and afterward he grew two hairs: רב said he is considered a סריס from the beginning. שמואל said he was a minor at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between רב and שמואל that connects to the punishment topic just mentioned. It asks whether a boy like this was punishable when he sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two hairs came late, after signs of a סריס had already appeared. רב says the hairs do not count: he was a סריס all along, so he is treated as an adult and liable for what he did. שמואל says the late hairs show he was just a slow-developing boy, so he was a minor at the time and not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fats, which carry a serious punishment
Two hairs: the sign of physical maturity
A minor, who cannot be punished

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the punishment topic רבי אלעזר just mentioned in action: the question of when a person becomes an adult decides whether he can be punished.

phrases.english: It was said:
If he ate forbidden fat,
from age twelve [and one day]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: until age eighteen,
and signs of a סריס appeared in him,
and after that he grew two hairs.
Rav said: He is considered a סריס from the beginning.
phrases.notes: The late hairs don't count, so he is treated as an adult and is liable.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: קָטָן הָיָה בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: He was a minor at that time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an argument about the punishment question that רבי אלעזר said the משנה in נדה deals with.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the boy is a סריס from the start and was liable. שמואל: the late hairs show he was a minor and not liable.

steps.title: רב יוסף Challenges Rav From the Fine
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues that by רב's logic, an אילונית should get the קנס according to רבי מאיר, which is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged this: According to רב, an אילונית according to רבי מאיר should receive the fine!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב's view by showing it leads to a strange result in the case of a woman who never matures, an אילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the קנס is paid only for a נערה, a girl in the middle stage between minor and full adult. An אילונית never shows signs, so she is treated as a minor and gets no קנס. But if, like רב says, someone who turns out underdeveloped is an adult from the beginning, she should count as a נערה from age twelve and get the קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who never develops normal signs of maturity
A fine paid to a girl who was violated, only when she is a נערה

phrases.english: Rav Yosef challenged it:
According to Rav, an אילונית according to Rabbi Meir
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר holds the fine is paid only for a girl in the middle stage, a נערה.

phrases.english: should get the fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's view from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one who turns out underdeveloped is treated that way from the beginning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an אילונית counts as an adult from the beginning, she should be a נערה at twelve and receive the קנס, but she does not.

steps.title: אביי: She Skips the Middle Stage
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that an אילונית goes straight from being a minor to being a full adult, so she is never a נערה and gets no קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: She goes out from her childhood straight to full adulthood.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב by explaining why an אילונית still gets no קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אילונית does not pass through the stage of נערות at all. She is a minor and then immediately a בוגרת, a full adult. Since the קנס is only for a נערה, she never qualifies, so רב's view causes no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Full adulthood, the stage after נערות

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר says רבי אליעזר never changed his mind, since the age rules are about punishment. רב and שמואל argue whether a late-maturing boy was liable, and אביי defends רב: an אילונית jumps from minor to full adult, so she gets no קנס.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
From her childhood she went out to full adulthood.
phrases.notes: She skips the middle stage of נערה, the only stage when the fine is paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִקַּטְנוּתָהּ יָצְתָה לְבֶגֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the stages: the אילונית never passes through נערות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If she is an adult from the beginning, she must have been a נערה and should get the קנס.
steps.terutzMaskana: She goes straight from minor to full adult, so she is never a נערה and gets no קנס.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי: no in-between stage for a סריס or an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף praises אביי's answer. The גמרא then cites a ברייתא: a סריס cannot become a בן סורר ומורה, and an אילונית cannot be judged as a נערה המאורסה, because she goes straight from being a minor to being a full adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to אביי: I wish all such excellent ideas were said in my name! As a ברייתא teaches: a סריס is not judged as a בן סורר ומורה, because a בן סורר ומורה is judged only when the hair of the 'lower beard' first appears. And an אילונית is not judged as a נערה המאורסה, because she goes straight from childhood to full adulthood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף accepts אביי's answer with warm praise. Then the גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what אביי said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed that an אילונית skips the נערה stage. The ברייתא states this outright: she 'goes from childhood to בגר.' It also gives a matching case for a male: a סריס never reaches the in-between stage, so he can never be a בן סורר ומורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'stubborn and rebellious son' of the תורה
When the hair of the 'lower beard' (pubic hair) appears
A betrothed young woman, a girl in the in-between stage

steps.whatToRemember: A סריס and an אילונית never pass through the in-between stage of youth. So laws that apply only to that stage, like בן סורר ומורה and נערה המאורסה, never apply to them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It settles רב יוסף's challenge from step 18. רב's view does not lead to giving an אילונית a קנס, because she is never a נערה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף speaking to אביי, reacting to the answer in step 19.

phrases.english: All such excellent matters as these
should be said in my name!
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A סריס is not judged
as a stubborn and rebellious son,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה נִידּוֹן
phrases.english: because a stubborn and rebellious son is not judged
except when the hair of the lower beard appears.
phrases.notes: 'Lower beard' means pubic hair. It marks the short stage just after a boy grows up, and a סריס never goes through it.

phrases.english: And an אילונית is not judged
as a betrothed young woman,
since from her childhood she went straight out to full adulthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל כִּי הָנֵי מִילֵּי מְעַלְּיָיתָא יִתְאַמְּרוּ מִשְּׁמַאי. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms אביי's answer from step 19 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that an אילונית skips the נערה stage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a סריס and בן סורר ומורה, and about an אילונית and נערה המאורסה.

steps.title: Wait until age twenty before acting on these signs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו rules that when someone shows the signs of a סריס, an אילונית, or a בן שמונה, we do not act on those signs until the person is twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: with the signs of a סריס, of an אילונית, or of a בן שמונה, we do not take any action based on them until the person reaches twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a new practical rule. Signs alone are not enough; we wait until the person is twenty before treating him or her as that type.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signs can show up early and may turn out to be misleading. So רבי אבהו sets age twenty as the point where we can rely on them. This fits the earlier discussion, where a person's status could change if two hairs grew later.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born in the eighth month of pregnancy
We do not take practical action based on them

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
The signs of a סריס, and of an אילונית,
and of a child born in the eighth month,
we do not take action based on them
until they are twenty years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: סִימָנֵי סָרִיס, וְאַיְלוֹנִית וּבֶן שְׁמֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory of the סריס and אילונית to a practical rule about when to rely on their signs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not act on the signs of a סריס, an אילונית, or a בן שמונה until age twenty.

steps.title: Can a baby born in the eighth month even survive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו: how can we speak of a בן שמונה reaching twenty? A ברייתא says such a baby is 'like a stone' and may not be moved on שבת, though his mother may bend over him and nurse him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a בן שמונה even live? But a ברייתא teaches: a בן שמונה is like a stone, and it is forbidden to move him. But his mother may bend over him and nurse him…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי אבהו's rule. It brings a ברייתא suggesting that a בן שמונה is not expected to live at all. The ברייתא continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's rule assumes a בן שמונה might live to twenty. But the ברייתא treats such a baby like a stone, an object you may not move on שבת, which implies he will not survive. That clashes with the idea of waiting until he is twenty.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a stone (here, an object you may not move on שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: The mother bending over to nurse him does not mean the baby is expected to live. She may nurse without picking him up, so the 'like a stone' rule still stands.

phrases.english: And can a child born in the eighth month live?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
A child born in the eighth month is like a stone,
phrases.notes: Like a stone on שבת: an object you may not move.

phrases.english: and it is forbidden to move him,
but his mother may bend over him
and nurse him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the בן שמונה part of רבי אבהו's rule in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's assumption that a בן שמונה could reach age twenty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats a בן שמונה like a stone on שבת, implying he will not survive. So how can we talk about waiting until he is twenty?
